# AI Dev Workspace — expanded context

> Shared Markdown task memory for developers who switch between Claude Code and Codex. Save decisions, next actions and dead ends in files you own; configured local hooks provide a task brief at session start. Install `pipx install ai-dev-workspace --pip-args='--pre'`, then run `ws start` in a Git repo to preview setup. Python 3.9+ CLI (`ws`) and local stdio MCP server; MIT licensed.

## Core command reference

Nine core CLI paths (ten invocations with cleanup): `ws start`, `ws remember`, `ws checkpoint`, `ws brief`, `ws task new`, `ws task list`, `ws task show`, `ws claim`, `ws release`. Flag variations, including `ws start --undo`, use the same path. The default MCP profile lists seven tools: `brief`, `find_task`, `read_task`, `checkpoint`, `remember`, `search_vault`, `add_lesson`. [Core reference](https://github.com/Alenroyfeild/ai-dev-workspace/blob/main/docs/COMMANDS.md#core).

## Stable — published 0.2.0

- Local Markdown task records, explicit `ws remember`, `ws checkpoint` and `ws brief`.
- Seven core MCP tools by default; other tools remain callable by name.
- Claude Code and Codex have historical [live sessions](https://github.com/Alenroyfeild/ai-dev-workspace/blob/main/docs/MEASUREMENTS.md#claude-and-cross-assistant-runs-2026-10-09).
  Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI and Antigravity are fixture-tested (CI).
  Linux: CI only; no live session on record. Windows: CI only.
- Only saved information is remembered; automatic transcript capture is best-effort.
- The optional guards pack is a safety net, not a security boundary.

## Stable workflow — published 0.2.0

```sh
pipx install ai-dev-workspace --pip-args='--pre'
cd path/to/your/git-repo
ws start
ws remember "Prices are integer cents"
ws checkpoint --status in_progress --next "Add the rate-limit check"
ws brief
```

`ws start` lists its files and asks before applying repo-local setup. Private
memory lives outside the code repo; generated local wiring is Git-excluded.
Opening the repo in a configured client supplies the task brief. Rerun `ws start`
for setup status; `ws start --undo` removes unchanged files that setup owns and
keeps user edits for review. Do not commit private memory or local client config.

Memory uses no background model calls. A plain handoff file can be sufficient;
historical synthetic results are not a claim of general productivity gains.
See the released Measurements page for later runs and the plain-HANDOFF caveat.

## Preview installation — Claude Code plugin

With the CLI installed and `ws start` completed in the repo, run in Claude Code:

```text
/plugin marketplace add Alenroyfeild/ai-dev-workspace
/plugin install ai-dev-workspace@ai-dev-workspace
```

This is our GitHub marketplace, not Anthropic's official directory. The beta.5
plugin has a live Claude check; setup and duplicate-wiring limits are described
in the [plugin guide](https://github.com/Alenroyfeild/ai-dev-workspace/blob/main/docs/ADVANCED.md#claude-code-plugin-preview).
Team sharing is Experimental (Preview, see below): share only reviewed notes with a private team repo.

## Experimental — outside the 1.0 promise

Commands beyond the core list are Experimental and may change or be removed. Experimental means: ships, but outside the 1.0 promise; the test level shown is today's. Full list with limits: [Experimental features](https://github.com/Alenroyfeild/ai-dev-workspace/blob/main/docs/EXPERIMENTAL.md).

- Delegation, workers, routing and orchestration; worker fallback chain (Preview) and gateway provider (Preview, local fake-server tests only).
- `ws audit` (Stable), `ws import claude-mem` (Preview), `ws digest` and the advisory behavior pack (Stable), `digest_file` (Preview), lesson promotion (Stable), Discipline pack (Stable), MCP Registry entry (Preview).
- Private team sharing (Preview): no hosted team check yet.
- Codex plugin and Cursor plugin (Preview), MCP plugin roots discovery (Preview), Codex SessionStart catch-up (Preview).
- Cursor, Copilot (VS Code), Gemini CLI and Antigravity: fixture-tested (CI); [live reports welcome](https://github.com/Alenroyfeild/ai-dev-workspace/issues/new?template=bug.yml).

## Released in 0.2.0

Labels in the release sections below are as published in that release; the current split between the 1.0 promise and Experimental is in the sections above.

- Experimental: `ws update --check` reports the installation type, local Git state and manual
  choices without pulling or changing branches. To upgrade: `ws update` (a package install
  prints `pipx upgrade ai-dev-workspace`), then `ws upgrade --dry-run`, `ws upgrade --yes`
  and `ws start` in each repo; running assistant sessions and MCP servers need a new
  session or a reload.
- Experimental: `ws upgrade` prints a migration result block, and `ws doctor` flags half-migrated stores.
- Stable: `ws start --undo --delete-memory` previews and, after confirmation, removes the
  recorded private workspace; plain `ws start --undo` still keeps memory.
- Experimental: `ws task next` selects and claims the next eligible task atomically.
- Measured (November 18, Codex `gpt-6-luna`, n=7 to 8 per arm): automatic capture is not
  reliable; the workspace arm passed 2/7 against 6/7 for a plain Markdown handoff, so
  save handoffs explicitly with `ws checkpoint` and `ws remember`.
- Stable: guards deny more git bypasses (config-env, `GIT_CONFIG_*`, aliases, abbreviated
  flags); they remain a safety net, not a security boundary.

## Released in beta.7

Labels in the release sections below are as published in that release; the current split between the 1.0 promise and Experimental is in the sections above.

- Stable: `ws lesson review [--days N]` lists old lesson date stamps for manual
  review; it is read-only and never changes or deletes saved lessons.
- Preview: Codex SessionStart catch-up recovers changed transcript content for the
  locally claimed task, including resumed turns without a callback; unsafe and
  ambiguous sources are skipped, and it is fixture-tested, not live-tested with
  Codex resume.
- Preview: MCP plugin servers discover a ws-started repo from client roots and stay
  inactive for unlinked or invalid roots; Codex offers no roots.
- Stable: guards parse git push option grammar, including abbreviations of
  --delete, --prune and --mirror; they remain a safety net, not a security boundary.

## Released in beta.6

- Stable: bounded compact MCP recall, read-only stack audit and the advisory behavior pack.
- Preview: opt-in digest advice is size-only; tool output is not compressed automatically.
- Preview: worker fallback runs only declared providers and read-only roles;
  gateway delegation is checked only with a local fake server and sends a redacted brief.
- Stable: lesson promotion drafts advice only; skills packaging is format-checked,
  without a verified third-party installer run.
- Preview: claude-mem import is fixture-tested against a checkpointed SQLite schema;
  newer schemas may not import.
- Preview: Antigravity rules, MCP and SessionStart/PreToolUse hooks are fixture-tested;
  there is no signed-in live proof or automatic capture.
- Preview: Claude Code plugin needs the CLI and `ws start`; not in Anthropic's
  directory, Windows untested. Codex plugin hooks need a trusted manual desktop install;
  no MCP in the plugin, no live hook proof. Cursor plugin is fixture-tested only,
  not submitted, with no verified install command. MCP plugin server roots discovery (Preview) activates only from client roots for already started workspaces and refuses others. [Plugin limits](https://github.com/Alenroyfeild/ai-dev-workspace/blob/main/docs/ADVANCED.md#plugin-runtime-packaging-preview).

## Coming next

Common Agent Plugins root manifest (PLG3) and Codex plugin MCP through roots (PLG5)
are parked and unavailable for Codex; codex-cli 0.155.1 offers no roots and cannot expand
plugin MCP paths, so use `ws start` for MCP. Clients that offer roots get the beta.7 Preview.
